output.summary: FY2026 records came from a commodity price rally, not business growth. Bushels fell 0.9%, handling revenue was flat, and the auditor attributes the margin gain to inventory appreciation. Peers with no new program grew similarly, and the co-op ranks 10th of 23 on net savings growth. The cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut from $905K to $612K while the deferred backlog tripled to $1.26M. Harlan Junction has critical insurer findings, a disconnected sensor, and an uninvestigated near-miss. Employees report concerns, but nothing changes. Drying and grading depend on an undocumented 63-year-old superintendent with no successor. The expansion case rests on FY2026 prices and unsourced volume, with no staffing or maintenance plan. Fix hazards, build succession, and rebuild the case before voting.
